memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports mild joint stiffness in mornings, able to attend online classes, no difficulty with ADLs.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4/5 (recall 3 items, clock draw normal).
falls: no falls in past 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 9 seconds (normal).
medicines: 6 regular (metformin 500 mg BD, combined oral contraceptive pill OD, methotrexate 10 mg weekly, folic acid 5 mg weekly, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD, prednisolone 5 mg OD) – polypharmacy, review against Beers criteria advised.
mood: denies low mood or anxiety; PHQ-2 not performed today.
carers: mother, Mrs Lakshmi Rao, provides occasional grocery help.
goal: "I want to keep studying and stay pain‑free to finish my degree."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
metformin 500 mg tablet, take orally twice daily after meals.
combined oral contraceptive pill (ethinylestradiol 0.03 mg + levonorgestrel 0.15 mg), take one tablet daily.
methotrexate 10 mg tablet, take orally once weekly on same day each week.
folic acid 5 mg tablet, take orally once weekly, same day as methotrexate.
hydroxychloroquine 200 mg tablet, take orally once daily.
prednisolone 5 mg tablet, take orally once daily in the morning.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum testosterone: 48 ng/dL (ref 15‑70).
LH:FSH ratio: 2.8 (LH 12 IU/L, FSH 4.3 IU/L) (ref <2.5 suggests PCOS).
HbA1c: 5.6% (ref 4‑5.6).
ESR: 22 mm/hr (ref 0‑20).
CRP: 8 mg/L (ref <5).
Rheumatoid factor: 28 IU/mL (ref <14).
Anti‑CCP: 45 U/mL (ref <20).
ALT: 28 U/L (ref 7‑35).
AST: 24 U/L (ref 10‑40).
ALP: 78 U/L (ref 30‑120).

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Pelvic ultrasound (transabdominal): bilateral ovaries enlarged, volume 10 mL each, multiple peripheral follicles (>12 per ovary), endometrial thickness 5 mm. No ovarian cyst >3 cm. Impression: polycystic ovarian morphology consistent with PCOS.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Allergy: sulfamethoxazole‑trimethoprim – rash and pruritus within 30 minutes of first dose, resolved with antihistamine.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more tired lately and my wrists ache after typing notes for my online lectures.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: notes increased wrist pain, difficulty typing for >30 minutes; still manages household chores.
cognition: Mini-Cog not repeated (last <12 months).
falls: no falls; gait slightly antalgic left wrist; timed up-and-go 10 seconds.
medicines: 6 regular – polypharmacy, continue current regimen, consider methotrexate dose review if LFTs rise.
mood: reports occasional frustration, denies depression.
carers: mother, Mrs Lakshmi Rao.
goal: "I want to reduce wrist pain so I can study longer without breaks."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
methotrexate dose increased to 15 mg once weekly.
folic acid unchanged 5 mg once weekly.
all other medicines unchanged.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Hand X‑ray (both wrists): periarticular osteopenia, mild joint space narrowing at distal radioulnar joints, no erosions. Consistent with early rheumatoid arthritis changes.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports improved wrist pain after methotrexate increase, able to type 45 minutes comfortably.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 3/5 (recall 2 items, clock draw mild abnormality) – positive screen, plan for full MoCA assessment.
falls: no falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 6 regular – polypharmacy, continue, discuss steroid taper.
mood: reports better mood, denies anxiety.
carers: mother, Mrs Lakshmi Rao.
goal: "I want to finish my final semester without medication side‑effects."

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum testosterone: 42 ng/dL (ref 15‑70).
LH:FSH ratio: 2.4 (LH 11 IU/L, FSH 4.6 IU/L).
HbA1c: 5.5% (ref 4‑5.6).
ESR: 14 mm/hr (ref 0‑20).
CRP: 4 mg/L (ref <5).
Rheumatoid factor: 22 IU/mL (ref <14).
Anti‑CCP: 30 U/mL (ref <20).
ALT: 22 U/L (ref 7‑35).
AST: 20 U/L (ref 10‑40).

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Patel, Endocrinology, for evaluation of persistent hyperandrogenism and menstrual irregularity despite OCPC. Request serum androgen panel and advice on OCPC continuation.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Endocrinology review: serum testosterone 44 ng/dL, DHEAS normal. Advised OCPC can be continued; consider adding spironolactone if hirsutism worsens. No immediate action needed.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports occasional flare of right knee pain after prolonged standing; otherwise functional.
cognition: MoCA performed 26/30 (normal).
falls: no falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 8 seconds.
medicines: 5 regular (prednisolone tapered to 2.5 mg OD, plan to stop) – now below polypharmacy threshold.
mood: stable.
carers: mother, Mrs Lakshmi Rao.
goal: "I want to stay active and pain‑free as I start work as a freelance tutor."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
prednisolone reduced to 2.5 mg once daily.
plan to discontinue prednisolone in 4 weeks if symptoms remain controlled.
all other medicines unchanged.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for review with Dr Nandini Kulkarni (D06) on 2026-10-02 at 10:30 am. Patient to bring medication list and pain diary.
